faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions from teams evaluating other observability and monitoring tools.
faq.q1: Is Middle Monitor an alternative to Datadog?
faq.a1: Yes. Middle Monitor unifies traces, metrics, logs and error tracking in one OpenTelemetry-native platform, with a free tier and transparent self-serve pricing as you scale — a common reason smaller engineering teams adopt it instead of Datadog.
faq.q2: How does Middle Monitor compare to Sentry for error tracking?
faq.a2: Error tracking is one of four signals Middle Monitor correlates natively, alongside traces, metrics and logs — so teams comparing Sentry, Rollbar or Bugsnag often adopt it to get error tracking and full-stack observability in a single platform.
faq.q3: Is there a simpler alternative to Icinga, Nagios or Zabbix?
faq.a3: Middle Monitor's agent captures CPU, memory, disk and network metrics automatically on Linux and macOS, without the manual check configuration typical of Icinga, Nagios or Zabbix, plus HTTP, ping, SQL, certificate and SNMP checks with built-in alerting.
faq.q4: Does Middle Monitor replace Dynatrace or New Relic?
faq.a4: Teams that find Dynatrace, New Relic or AppDynamics priced and scoped for large enterprises use Middle Monitor for the same core APM workflow — distributed tracing, root cause analysis and alerting — on a simpler, self-serve platform.
faq.q5: Can Middle Monitor replace a Prometheus, Grafana or Jaeger setup?
faq.a5: Middle Monitor is OpenTelemetry-native, so it ingests the same trace, metric and log data you'd otherwise send to a self-hosted Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger or Zipkin stack, correlated automatically in one place.
faq.q6: Is there an alternative to Splunk or the ELK stack for logs?
faq.a6: Middle Monitor collects application logs through the same SDK that handles your traces and errors, and each log carries the trace id of the request that produced it — so you move from a log line to the full request instead of correlating timestamps by hand across a separate search cluster like Splunk or an Elastic (ELK) stack.
faq.q7: Is there an alternative to Pingdom, UptimeRobot or Better Stack for uptime monitoring?
faq.a7: Middle Monitor includes HTTP, ping, SQL, certificate and SNMP checks with incident alerting in the same platform as your traces and logs, so you don't need a separate uptime tool like Pingdom, UptimeRobot or Better Stack.
faq.q8: What data is sent to the AI for root cause analysis?
faq.a8: A minimal payload, sent to Groq: the error name and message, file and line, service name, timestamp, and the HTTP method and URL of the failing request — plus the status, type and target of a failing check. Request bodies, HTTP headers and organization identifiers are stripped before the call, and log contents are never transmitted: only their count is. Infrastructure explanations such as CPU or disk saturation are produced by deterministic rules and never reach a model at all.
faq.q9: Is Middle Monitor open source? Can I self-host it?
faq.a9: Yes. The platform, the agent and the SDKs are on GitHub (github.com/middle-monitor/middle-monitor) under the FSL-1.1-ALv2 license: free to use, modify and self-host for any purpose except offering it as a competing commercial service, and each release becomes Apache 2.0 after two years. One Docker Compose file starts the whole stack, and a self-hosted instance has no plan limits.

labels.threshold_hint_errors: If the number of errors exceeds this threshold over 1 minute, an alert is sent.
labels.threshold_hint_traces: If a request duration exceeds this threshold, an alert is sent.
labels.threshold_hint_default: Defines from which value the metric is considered failed.
labels.threshold_hint_cert: Send an alert if the certificate expires within N days. Defaults: Warning at 30 days, Critical at 7 days.
labels.threshold_hint_sql: Critical if connection latency exceeds this value. Warning alerts are managed automatically (slow queries, connections, locks, bloat).
labels.threshold_hint_snmp: If the OID value returned exceeds these thresholds, a Warning or Critical alert is sent. Without a threshold, the check only verifies device availability.

notice.title: Legal Notice
notice.intro: This page identifies who operates the middlemonitor.io website and the Middle Monitor platform, and how to reach us.
notice.publisher_body:
The middlemonitor.io website and the Middle Monitor platform are published and operated by Middle Monitor, an independent software publisher established in the European Union.
Up-to-date publisher and registration details are available on request through the contact form.
notice.contact_body: For any question about the service, including legal, billing and privacy requests, use the contact form on this site. We answer every message as soon as possible.
notice.hosting_body: The platform and all customer data are hosted on servers located in the European Union. Data does not leave the European Union in the normal operation of the service.
notice.ip_body: The Middle Monitor name, logo and the content of this website are the property of the publisher. The SDKs and the monitoring agent are distributed under the license published in their respective source repositories.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Middle Monitor is an observability platform: our customers send us operational data about their own systems so they can monitor them. This policy explains what data we handle, why, where it is stored and what rights you have.
privacy.account_body: When you create an account we collect your name, email address and a password. Passwords are stored hashed and are never readable by us. Organization details you provide (organization name, members, roles) are stored to operate your workspace.
privacy.telemetry_body:
The core of the service is telemetry that your systems send through the agent, the SDKs or the API: traces, metrics, logs, error reports, profiles and host information.
You control entirely what is sent. Telemetry may embed personal data if your applications include it in logs or error messages; we process such data on your behalf and on your instructions, as a processor.
Do not send secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens) in telemetry. Configure your applications to filter sensitive values before they reach the SDK.
The HTTP middlewares record the caller's IP address on the request logs they write, which is what makes an automated scan recognisable. The address is anonymized on your own server before anything is sent: only the network is kept, the host part is dropped. Set MIDDLE_MONITOR_CLIENT_IP to full to record whole addresses, or to off to record none — recording full addresses is your decision as controller of that data, and needs its own legal basis and a mention in your own privacy policy.
privacy.billing_body: Paid plans are billed through Stripe, our payment processor. Card details are entered on and stored by Stripe; we never see or store your full card number. We keep invoicing records as required by law.
privacy.contact_form_body: When you use the contact form we receive the name, email address and message you submit, and we use them only to answer you.
privacy.analytics_body: We measure site traffic with a self-hosted, cookieless analytics tool. It collects aggregated usage data only (pages viewed, referrer, browser family) and cannot identify you or follow you across other sites. No data is shared with advertising networks.
privacy.hosting_body: All customer data is stored and processed on servers located in the European Union.
privacy.retention_body:
Telemetry is retained according to your plan (7 days on the Free plan, 30 days on Pro, configurable on custom plans) and is then deleted automatically.
Account data is kept for as long as your account exists and deleted when the account is closed. Invoicing records are kept for the duration required by law.
privacy.sharing_body:
We never sell personal data. We share data only with the subprocessors needed to run the service:
- Stripe, for payment processing;
- our transactional email provider, to deliver alert and account emails.
Each subprocessor only receives the data required for its role.
privacy.security_body: All traffic to and inside the platform uses TLS. Passwords are hashed, API access is authenticated with scoped tokens, and access to production systems is restricted.
privacy.cookies_body: We set no advertising or third-party tracking cookies. The application stores authentication tokens and your language preference in your browser's local storage, strictly to keep you signed in and remember your settings.
privacy.rights_body: Under the GDPR you can request access to, rectification, erasure or portability of your personal data, and object to or restrict its processing. Send any request through the contact form; we answer within the legal timeframe. You can also lodge a complaint with your local supervisory authority.
privacy.changes_body: We will update this page when our practices change and adjust the date at the top. Significant changes are announced to account owners by email.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of the Middle Monitor platform and website. By creating an account or using the service you accept them.
terms.service_body: Middle Monitor is an observability platform: it ingests traces, metrics, logs, errors and profiling data from your systems through an agent, SDKs and an API, and provides dashboards, alerting and analysis on top of that data.
terms.accounts_body: You must provide accurate information when registering and keep your credentials secure. You are responsible for activity under your account and for the members you invite into your organization.
terms.data_body:
You own the telemetry you send. You grant us the right to store and process it solely to provide the service. We do not use customer telemetry for anything else and we delete it per the retention rules of your plan.
You are responsible for ensuring the data you send complies with the law and does not contain secrets or personal data you are not allowed to share.
terms.billing_body: The Free plan is available at no cost within its limits. Paid plans are billed monthly through Stripe. You can upgrade, downgrade or cancel at any time; changes apply to the next billing period. Fees already paid are non-refundable except where the law requires otherwise.
terms.availability_body: We work to keep the service available and monitor it continuously, but it is provided "as is" without a guaranteed service level. Planned maintenance is announced in advance whenever possible.
terms.liability_body: To the extent permitted by law, our total liability for any claim related to the service is limited to the amounts you paid us in the twelve months preceding the claim. We are not liable for indirect damages such as lost profits, or for lost data caused by circumstances outside our control.
terms.termination_body: You can close your account at any time. We may suspend or terminate accounts that violate these terms, after notice when practicable. On termination your telemetry is deleted according to the retention rules.
terms.changes_body: We may update these terms; the date at the top reflects the latest version. Material changes are announced to account owners by email before they take effect.
terms.law_body: These terms are governed by French law. Any dispute that cannot be resolved amicably falls under the jurisdiction of the competent French courts.
